subject: Energy
title: Fukushima Daiichi
description: Learn Fukushima Daiichi in one minute.

hook.text: On March 11, 2011, a magnitude 9 earthquake and tsunami struck Japan—triggering meltdowns at three Fukushima reactors.

buildup.text: The reactors shut down as designed during the quake—but the 15-meter tsunami flooded backup diesel generators.

discovery.text: Without cooling, fuel melted in three cores—hydrogen explosions blew apart the reactor buildings.

twist.text: No one died from radiation at Fukushima—but the evacuation of 154,000 people caused significant hardship and deaths.

climax.text: Japan shut all 54 reactors for review—the disaster reshaped global nuclear policy and accelerated safety upgrades.

punchline.text: Nature overwhelmed the backup—and the nuclear world was changed.

quiz.question: What caused the Fukushima meltdowns?
options: The tsunami flooded backup cooling systems
